Two steps ask a language model: **AI: ask a model** (`ai.chat`) for one answer,
and **AI: run an agent** (`ai.agent`) for a model that works toward a goal using
your other workflows as its tools.

The model is yours. A credential of type **AI model** says where it runs and
which one to use, and nothing in Cascade sends a prompt anywhere else. There is
no hosted service, no account with us and nothing to turn on: run a model on a
box you own, or use a hosted service with your own key. Every call goes through
the egress policy like any other outbound call, so a model on your plant
network has to be allowed on purpose (`HOTLOOP_CASCADE_EGRESS_ALLOW`, by host
name or CIDR).

## The credential

| Field | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|
| Protocol | `openai` (the default) speaks the OpenAI chat completions protocol, which is also what Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp and LM Studio serve. `anthropic` speaks Anthropic's messages protocol. |
| Server URL | Empty uses the provider's own (`https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://api.anthropic.com`). For a local model, its address with the version path, like `http://ollama.plant.lan:11434/v1`. |
| API key | A secret, sealed in the vault. Empty for a local model. |
| Model name | The model to ask, like `qwen2.5:1.5b` or `gpt-4.1`. A step can override it. |

## Ask a model

```yaml
- name: Summarize
  type: ai.chat
  version: 1
  params:
    system: You write one plain sentence for a shift handover.
    prompt: "Alarm on {{ item.json.line }}: {{ item.json.message }}"
    temperature: 0
  credentials:
    model: my-model
```

The answer goes under `ai` on the item (change it with `into`):
`ai.text`, `ai.model`, `ai.finishReason` and `ai.usage.inputTokens` and
`outputTokens`. With `output: json` the model is asked for a JSON object, a
`schema` makes servers that enforce one hold it to that shape, and the parsed
object is in `ai.json`. A reply that isn't JSON stops the step with what the
model wrote.

## Run an agent

```yaml
- name: Find out
  type: ai.agent
  version: 1
  params:
    prompt: "What is oven {{ item.json.oven }} at? Use the tool, then answer in degrees C."
    tools:
      - name: read_oven
        description: Reads the current temperature of an oven, in degrees C.
        workflow: 0197b2a4-....
        parameters:
          type: object
          properties: {oven: {type: integer}}
          required: [oven]
    maxTurns: 6
  credentials:
    model: my-model
```

Each tool is a workflow in the same project that starts with **When another
workflow runs this one**. When the model asks for a tool, Cascade runs that
workflow with the arguments the model gave as one item, waits for it, and hands
its last output back to the model as the tool's result. A failed tool goes back
as an error the model can read and react to. A name the step never offered goes
back the same way. This repeats until the model answers without asking for
another tool, or `maxTurns` (1 to 50, default 10) is reached and the step stops.

Between turns the run waits in the database, not in a worker, so a tool that
takes an hour costs nothing and a restart loses only the turn in flight. Each
item is its own conversation, and the result is on the item under `ai`: `text`,
`turns`, `toolCalls` (the names, in order), `model` and `usage`.

Because a tool is a workflow, it has the permissions of its own project and
its own credentials, and shows up in the executions list like any other run.
Give an agent only the tools you would give a person on that shift.
